text:
Cutter Gauthier scored three times for ANA, and the Ducks needed every one of them. Gauthier, drafted fifth overall by the Flyers in 2022 and later traded to Anaheim, had two power-play goals and a third at even strength, and finished with six shots on goal. His line mate Beckett Sennecke assisted on all three of his goals and added a fourth helper on Mikael Granlund's opener.

The 5-4 final flatters ANA. By expected goals (the quality of chances each side created), VAN led 2.74 to 2.53, and our deserved-to-win figure, the share of simulated replays of every shot that a team wins, gave VAN 62 percent. At even strength the gap was wider, 1.95 to 1.34. ANA went 3 for 3 on the power play, VAN went 2 for 4, and Leo Carlsson's shorthanded goal came on a 4 percent chance. That one made it 3-1 in the second period. VAN had the third period almost to itself, out-chancing ANA 0.99 to 0.34, and Jake DeBrusk scored twice in it, a power-play backhand and a deflection. The comeback stopped one goal short.

Kevin Lankinen allowed 2.9 goals more than the chances he faced should have produced, and that gap decided a game VAN controlled. Laurent Brossoit was also below expectation by 1.26 goals but stopped Paul Cotter's best look, a 23 percent chance in the second. The two teams have now split one overtime and one regulation game this season: VAN won the first meeting on Oct. 27, 6-5 in OT, and ANA took this one. The facts give no streaks or records for either club.
